hook.line: Vale texts about everything in capitals and stretched letters, and Tomás keeps missing the tone. Colombians turn the volume up with little prefixes and doubled words, and in chat they stretch a word to show what they really mean.

examples.es: Quiero un tinto tinto, sin leche.
examples.en: I want a proper black coffee, no milk.

rule:
English says *really* or *so*. Spanish glues a prefix onto the adjective.

*super-*: *superbueno*, *superfácil*, glued on. You'll also see it as its own word with an accent: *súper bueno*.
*re-*: *rebueno*, *rebonito*, or in chat *re bueno*. Very Colombian and Mexican, and a bit more casual.

To say the real thing, say the word twice: *café café* is proper coffee, not the instant kind.

In chat, stretched letters carry the tone. *Pueees* is polite disagreement or doubt. *Bueeeno* is reluctance. *Poooor fa* is pleading. Use these with friends only, never in a formal email.
smallPrint: Teachers call the prefixes *intensificadores* and the doubled word *reduplicación*.

options: The soup is a bit tasty.
The exam is a bit easy.
My sister is really good people.
My sister is a good boss.
They make two black coffees here.
They make a proper black coffee here.
They make a bad black coffee here.
